finding.web_files_extra.oidc_alg_none: The identity provider advertises the “none” signing algorithm for its tokens: an unsigned token might be accepted.
finding.web_files_extra.permissive_polic: Overly permissive cross-domain policy (all domains allowed): {files}.
module.web_files_extra.checks: Looks for conventional public files: humans.txt, ads.txt, app-ads.txt, web manifest, .well-known (OpenID, OAuth, change-password, assetlinks, apple-app-site-association, host-meta, NodeInfo, gpc), crossdomain.xml and clientaccesspolicy.xml, validating their content.
module.web_files_extra.fix:
If `crossdomain.xml` or `clientaccesspolicy.xml` allows every domain (`*` or `permitted-cross-domain-policies="all"`), delete the file: Flash and Silverlight are no longer supported. If an old client still depends on it, limit the list to trusted domains only.
If `openid-configuration` or `oauth-authorization-server` announces the `none` algorithm in `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`, remove it from your identity server settings, keep strong algorithms such as `RS256` or `ES256`, and check that your applications reject any unsigned token.
In those same files, check that `issuer` and the endpoint addresses (`authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`) start with `https://`, never `http://`.
For each file found (`humans.txt`, `ads.txt`, manifest, `assetlinks.json`, `apple-app-site-association`, `host-meta`, NodeInfo), check that it is intended and up to date, and remove what no longer belongs (old app, terminated vendor, personal name or address).
In `assetlinks.json` and `apple-app-site-association`, only list the apps you actually publish: these files tie your site to those apps. In `ads.txt`, only keep vendors under an active contract.
If the site has accounts, publish `/.well-known/change-password` as a redirect to your password change page: password managers use it.
Run the scan again: no more permissive cross-domain policy, no more `none` algorithm.
module.web_files_extra.title: Informational files and .well-known
module.web_files_extra.why: These files describe the site, its apps and its identity providers. An overly broad cross-domain policy (crossdomain.xml with “*”) lets any site read its data.
